newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late with cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still down late with cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained lower late Friday in lackluster activity, still pressured by softer February physical prices amid forecasts for mostly-mild U.S. temperatures next week, sources said.
At 1415 EST, March slipped 6.1 cents to $2.425 per million British thermal units, while April was three cents lower at $2.185. Most others were steady to down two cents.

"It's trying to hold, but people are thinking winter is over and I think we're going to challenge the $2.35 area and possibly break into the teens (basis March)," said one East Coast trader, noting bearish weather forecasts near-term.

According to Weather Services Corp, temperatures for most of the U.S. are expected to return to more moderate levels by next week, with weather in Texas and the Southeast forecast to climb to above normal.
With adequate stocks in the East, many said only a sustained cold snap in the Midwest and Texas could drive the complex much higher.
Technically, traders pegged support in March in the $2.40 area and then at the December 30 low of $2.35. Resistance was seen at $2.70 and $2.80.
In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped about a dime into the mid-$2.70s. Midcon pipes tumbled more than 20 cents to about the $2.50 level. New York city gate gas skidded 15 cents into the mid-$3.40s.
NYMEX said 7,646 Hub contracts traded by 1130 EST.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1155 EST.
On the KCBT, March was still down by five cents at $2.14, while April remained two cents lower at $1.93. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.1 cents to 28.5 cents (NYMEX premium).
